sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Deal.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Deal》节目。

sentences.en: Earlier this month, a second person was cured of HIV, something that after three decades of fighting for a cure, scientists and activists had almost given up on.
sentences.zh: 本月早些时候，第二位艾滋病患者被治愈了，这在经过三十年抗击艾滋病的斗争后，科学家和活动家们几乎已经放弃了希望。

sentences.en: How we got here.
sentences.zh: 我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月21日，星期四。

sentences.en: So Peter Staley, when did you first hear about HIV and AIDS?
sentences.zh: 那么彼得·斯泰利，你第一次听说HIV和艾滋病是什么时候？

sentences.en: Where were you?
sentences.zh: 当时你在哪里？

sentences.en: And what was going on in your life?
sentences.zh: 你的生活中发生了什么？

sentences.en: I think I first heard about AIDS probably a year into the crisis, 1982.
sentences.zh: 我想我大概是在危机爆发一年后，也就是1982年第一次听说艾滋病。

sentences.en: It's mysterious, it's deadly, and it's baffling medical science.
sentences.zh: 它神秘、致命，且让医学界感到困惑。

sentences.en: Like the first mainstream television report.
sentences.zh: 就像第一次主流电视报道那样。

sentences.en: The lifestyle of some male homosexuals has triggered an epidemic.
sentences.zh: 某些男同性恋者的生活方式引发了一场流行病。

sentences.en: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, or the acronym by which it's frequently identified, AIDS.
sentences.zh: 获得性免疫缺陷综合征，也就是常说的缩写词——艾滋病。

sentences.en: And I'm still in college at Oberlin.
sentences.zh: 那时我还在欧柏林学院上学。

sentences.en: Researchers are now studying blood and other samples from the victims, trying to learn what is causing the disease.
sentences.zh: 研究人员正在研究来自患者的血液和其他样本，试图找出导致这种疾病的原因。

sentences.en: So far, they have had no luck.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他们一无所获。

sentences.en: You know, it seemed like this strange mystery.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这看起来像是一个奇怪的谜团。

sentences.en: I'm not sure how applicable it felt to my life.
sentences.zh: 我不确定它与我的生活有多大关联。

sentences.en: Investigators have examined the habits of homosexuals for clues.
sentences.zh: 调查人员检查了同性恋者的习惯以寻找线索。

sentences.en: I was in the fast lane at one time, in terms of the way that I lived my life, and now I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我曾经在生活方式上走过快车道，但现在不是了。

sentences.en: I was a closeted homosexual.
sentences.zh: 我当时是一名深柜同性恋者。

sentences.en: Certainly wasn't hearing about it on campus at all.
sentences.zh: 在校园里我根本没听说过这件事。

sentences.en: And then I came to New York in about April of 83 for this new job on Wall Street, and had my first conversations with other gay men.
sentences.zh: 后来我在83年4月左右来到纽约从事华尔街的新工作，并第一次与其他男同性恋者进行了交流。

sentences.en: And at least in my generation, the very young 20-somethings, often closeted, it still seemed remote.
sentences.zh: 至少在我这一代，那些非常年轻的二十多岁的人，通常都是深柜，它看起来仍然很遥远。

sentences.en: We were telling each other that it was mostly happening in older gay men, and those who had been highly, highly prolific in their sexuality.
sentences.zh: 我们当时互相说，这主要发生在年长的男同性恋者身上，以及那些性生活非常、非常频繁的人身上。

sentences.en: So, fast forward a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 那么，快进几年。

sentences.en: To begin with, AIDS was just an obscure medical curiosity.
sentences.zh: 起初，艾滋病只是一个晦涩的医学奇闻。

sentences.en: I'm now a bond trader on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 我现在是华尔街的一名债券交易员。

sentences.en: A strange illness affecting a handful of homosexuals and drug abusers in American cities.
sentences.zh: 一种影响美国城市中少数同性恋者和吸毒者的奇怪疾病。

sentences.en: Today, the virus has claimed thousands of lives and threatens millions more.
sentences.zh: 今天，这种病毒夺去了成千上万人的生命，并威胁着更多人的生命。

sentences.en: When the AIDS alarm sounded four years ago, most people knew little or nothing about the disease, much less knew anyone who had it.
sentences.zh: 当四年前艾滋病警报响起时，大多数人对这种疾病知之甚少，甚至一无所知，更不用说认识任何感染者了。

sentences.en: Now, as the number of cases doubles every six months, that profile is changing.
sentences.zh: 现在，随着病例数量每六个月翻一番，这种状况正在改变。

sentences.en: And AIDS has finally become a massive story in the country.
sentences.zh: 艾滋病终于成为了全国关注的重大新闻。

sentences.en: Some might be led to believe that the disease is leveling off.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能会被误导，认为这种疾病正在趋于平稳。

sentences.en: It is not.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And not in a good way.
sentences.zh: 而且情况不容乐观。

sentences.en: Many researchers would argue that the number of cases is actually 10 times higher than those reported by the Centers for Disease Control.
sentences.zh: 许多研究人员会认为，实际病例数比美国疾病控制与预防中心报告的数字高出10倍。

sentences.en: You know, they should just come out and tell people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们应该直接站出来告诉人们真相。

sentences.en: The country was in a panic.
sentences.zh: 全国陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: You know, got everybody's skin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让每个人都感到毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: There were cover stories on all the national magazines about AIDS.
sentences.zh: 所有全国性杂志都刊登了关于艾滋病的封面故事。

sentences.en: Parents were pulling their kids out of schools.
sentences.zh: 家长们纷纷让孩子退学。

sentences.en: If there were rumors about a child having HIV.
sentences.zh: 如果传言说某个孩子感染了HIV。

sentences.en: These people are raising money and signing petitions in a fight to keep Ryan White out of their school.
sentences.zh: 这些人正在筹款并签署请愿书，试图阻止瑞安·怀特进入他们的学校。

sentences.en: He has a spill on a table, a chair.
sentences.zh: 他把东西洒在桌子或椅子上。

sentences.en: Your daughter comes in, catches it.
sentences.zh: 你女儿进来，接触到了。

sentences.en: What's to say she is not going to get it?
sentences.zh: 谁能保证她不会被传染？

sentences.en: And I sat down with my kind of newish boyfriend at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时我和我那刚交往不久的男朋友坐在一起。

sentences.en: Breakfast is served.
sentences.zh: 早餐准备好了。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We're almost out of shaving cream.
sentences.zh: 我们的剃须膏快用完了。

sentences.en: No, okay.
sentences.zh: 不，好吧。

sentences.en: To watch the very first television movie about the subject, which was called An Early FroSt.
sentences.zh: 观看关于这个主题的第一部电视电影，片名叫《早霜》。

sentences.en: So, how'd it go with your folks?
sentences.zh: 那么，你和你父母谈得怎么样？

sentences.en: And Aidan Quinn was the star.
sentences.zh: 艾丹·奎因是主演。

sentences.en: You didn't tell him that.
sentences.zh: 你没告诉他那个。

sentences.en: He played a closeted gay man.
sentences.zh: 他扮演了一个深柜男同性恋者。

sentences.en: Look, I don't have the same relationship with my parents that you have with yours, okay?
sentences.zh: 听着，我和父母的关系跟你和你的父母不一样，好吗？

sentences.en: I don't talk about sex with them.
sentences.zh: 我不跟他们谈性。

sentences.en: They don't talk about sex with me.
sentences.zh: 他们也不跟我谈性。

sentences.en: Who is talking about sex?
sentences.zh: 谁在谈性了？

sentences.en: Talking about us.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论我们自己。

sentences.en: Who gets hit by AIDS with PCP pneumonia, which was the common killer back then.
sentences.zh: 谁会因为患上PCP肺炎而感染艾滋病，那可是当时常见的杀手。

sentences.en: And I'm sitting there watching this thing, and I've got a bad cough.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那里看着这部片子，我当时咳嗽得很厉害。

sentences.en: Why don't you go home?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不回家呢？

sentences.en: I was hoping you'd say that.
sentences.zh: 我正希望你这么说。

sentences.en: How about you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: I want to check these sites firSt.
sentences.zh: 我想先检查一下这些站点。

sentences.en: And Aidan Quinn is coughing away, acting like he has PCP pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 艾丹·奎因一直在咳嗽，演得就像他得了PCP肺炎一样。

sentences.en: And during one of the commercial breaks,
sentences.zh: 在其中一个广告插播期间，

sentences.en: I'm hacking away, and this boyfriend leans over and says, you sound just like him.
sentences.zh: 我咳个不停，这个男朋友凑过来对我说，你听起来跟他一模一样。

sentences.en: Fortunately, I had a gay doctor in New York City, a guy named Dan William.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我在纽约市有一位同性恋医生，名叫丹·威廉。

sentences.en: At that point, Dan was so paranoid about the health of all his patients that if you went in there with anything, he would run a CBC, a complete blood count,
sentences.zh: 当时，丹对所有病人的健康状况都非常敏感，如果你带着任何不适去看病，他都会为你做全血细胞计数，

sentences.en: just a regular blood teSt.
sentences.zh: 也就是常规血液检查。

sentences.en: 48 hours after that appointment,
sentences.zh: 那次预约48小时后，

sentences.en: I got a call from his nurse while I was at my trading desk.
sentences.zh: 我在交易台工作时接到了他护士的电话。

sentences.en: I remember it very clearly.
sentences.zh: 我记得非常清楚。

sentences.en: It was a Friday morning.
sentences.zh: 那是一个周五的早晨。

sentences.en: And he said, there's an abnormality on your test, and Dan would like you to come in for some more blood work.
sentences.zh: 他说，你的检查结果有异常，丹希望你过来做进一步的血液检查。

sentences.en: And I pressed him, and he said, it might be indication of AIDS.
sentences.zh: 我追问他，他说，这可能是艾滋病的迹象。

sentences.en: Right then and there, I just knew that that's what it was.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我立刻知道那就是艾滋病。

sentences.en: I felt like I'd been handed a, you know, a death sentence.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己仿佛被判了死刑。

sentences.en: That's kind of the classic story.
sentences.zh: 这算是经典的故事了。

sentences.en: I sat down on my bed and started crying because I realized how screwed I was.
sentences.zh: 我坐在床上开始哭泣，因为我意识到自己完了。

sentences.en: So at that point, it became a game of where can I find treatments to buy me a year, some months, a few years, buy me some time.
sentences.zh: 所以在那一刻，这变成了一场寻找治疗方法的游戏，希望能为我争取一年、几个月、几年，为我争取一些时间。

sentences.en: And what was the answer?
sentences.zh: 答案是什么呢？

sentences.en: Where could you and did you go for treatments at this phase?
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你去了哪里寻求治疗？

sentences.en: There was nothing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。

sentences.en: There were no treatments approved at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时没有任何获批的治疗方法。

sentences.en: But the first thing I did after my diagnosis was go home and tell my family.
sentences.zh: 但我确诊后做的第一件事就是回家告诉我的家人。

sentences.en: And they rallied to my side.
sentences.zh: 他们都站在我这边支持我。

sentences.en: It was just wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: So I had this initial support group, but I still felt very alone.
sentences.zh: 所以我有了最初的支持小组，但我仍然感到非常孤独。

sentences.en: I hadn't met another person with HIV.
sentences.zh: 我还没有见过其他感染HIV的人。

sentences.en: So I finally got myself to an HIV support group at GMHC.
sentences.zh: 所以我最终去了GMHC的一个HIV支持小组。

sentences.en: Gay men's health crisis.
sentences.zh: 男同性恋者健康危机组织。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I actually didn't like what I was hearing.
sentences.zh: 但我其实并不喜欢我所听到的。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: They were living in the stigma.
sentences.zh: 他们生活在耻辱之中。

sentences.en: They were all saying they had stopped having sex.
sentences.zh: 他们都说他们已经停止了性生活。

sentences.en: They felt like they were walking around with a scarlet letter.
sentences.zh: 他们感觉自己像是在身上贴着耻辱的标签。

sentences.en: They were filled with fear about dying any day.
sentences.zh: 他们整天充满对死亡的恐惧。

sentences.en: They were in full trauma mode rather than fight mode.
sentences.zh: 他们处于完全的创伤模式，而不是战斗模式。

sentences.en: But there was this one guy across from me who spoke up and he was a character.
sentences.zh: 但坐在我对面有一个人发言了，他很有个性。

sentences.en: He was in leather and he had kind of spiked hair and very goth.
sentences.zh: 他穿着皮衣，留着尖刺状的发型，非常哥特。

sentences.en: And he said, well, I don't know what you're all talking about.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不明白你们在说什么。

sentences.en: I'm not going to stop living.
sentences.zh: 我不会停止生活。

sentences.en: And my eyes widened and it's like, yeah, this is the guy I got to get to know.
sentences.zh: 我的眼睛睁大了，心想，没错，这就是我必须结识的人。

sentences.en: His name was Griffin Gold.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫格里芬·戈尔德。

sentences.en: And it was just such great luck because he was one of the leaders of the self-empowerment movement of people with AIDS in the country.
sentences.zh: 这真是太幸运了，因为他是全国艾滋病患者自我赋权运动的领导者之一。

sentences.en: And he started tying me into this early activism.
sentences.zh: 他开始带我参与早期的活动。

sentences.en: And then all of us got lucky six months after that when ACT UP was born.
sentences.zh: 六个月后，当ACT UP成立时，我们所有人都很幸运。

sentences.en: There's a new AIDS death every half hour.
sentences.zh: 每半小时就有一个艾滋病患者死亡。

sentences.en: There's a new HIV infection every single minute.
sentences.zh: 每一分钟都有一个新的HIV感染病例。

sentences.en: ACT UP was really in response to a call by Larry Kramer.
sentences.zh: ACT UP实际上是为了响应拉里·克莱默的号召。

sentences.en: I think the ground squell of new chapters of new members is very similar to what happened during the Vietnam War where people got so angry at the government
sentences.zh: 我认为新分部、新成员的涌现与越南战争期间发生的情况非常相似，当时人们对政府感到非常愤怒，

sentences.en: that they were forced into this frustration.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们被迫陷入这种挫败感中。

sentences.en: Saying that people weren't aware enough and weren't fighting back.
sentences.zh: 他们说人们不够警觉，没有进行反击。

sentences.en: And he wanted a political response.
sentences.zh: 他想要一种政治回应。

sentences.en: We are in the middle of a plague!
sentences.zh: 我们正处于瘟疫之中！

sentences.en: And I had this crazy first year with ACT UP where I was still working on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 我在ACT UP度过了疯狂的第一年，当时我还在华尔街工作。

sentences.en: So I had to keep my activism kind of in the closet, as it were.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不把我的活动隐藏起来，可以说是处于“柜中”。

sentences.en: And then after about a year of that, the game was kind of up.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后，游戏结束了。

sentences.en: My CD4 count crashed below 200.
sentences.zh: 我的CD4细胞计数降到了200以下。

sentences.en: In my head, I knew from the science that that usually would start kind of this clock.
sentences.zh: 在我的脑海里，我从科学知识中知道，这通常意味着倒计时开始了。

sentences.en: That people who had less than 200 CD4 cells were dying of AIDS in about two years.
sentences.zh: CD4细胞少于200的人大约会在两年内死于艾滋病。

sentences.en: So I felt a clock had started.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉时钟已经开始走动了。

sentences.en: And I only had two years left.
sentences.zh: 我只剩下两年时间了。

sentences.en: I couldn't keep trying to trade bonds on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 我无法再继续在华尔街交易债券了。

sentences.en: So the very next morning after that CD4 count, I walked into my boss's office and told him everything and said, I'm walking out of here now and this is my last day.
sentences.zh: 所以CD4计数出来后的第二天早上，我走进老板的办公室，告诉了他一切，并说，我现在就要离开，这是我的最后一天。

sentences.en: And so what do you do next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来你做了什么？

sentences.en: I go full in on ACT UP.
sentences.zh: 我全身心地投入到ACT UP中。

sentences.en: Gay people and straight people, black people and white people, men and women will hear the story that once there was a terrible disease
sentences.zh: 同性恋者和异性恋者，黑人和白人，男人和女人，都将听到这个故事：曾经有一种可怕的疾病，

sentences.en: and that a brave group of people stood up and fought and in some cases died so that others might live and be free.
sentences.zh: 一群勇敢的人站出来抗争，在某些情况下甚至献出了生命，只为了让其他人能够活着并获得自由。

sentences.en: It became my church.
sentences.zh: 它成了我的教堂。

sentences.en: It became my family.
sentences.zh: 它成了我的家人。

sentences.en: It became my social life.
sentences.zh: 它成了我的社交生活。

sentences.en: And it started keeping me alive.
sentences.zh: 它开始让我活下去。

sentences.en: And after we kick the shit out of this disease, I intend to be alive, to kick the shit out of the system so that this will never happen again.
sentences.zh: 等我们彻底击败这种疾病后，我打算继续活下去，去彻底击败这个体制，让这种事永远不再发生。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Two weeks after I left Wall Street,
sentences.zh: 在我离开华尔街两周后，

sentences.en: I got arrested on Wall Street for ACT UP's one-year anniversary.
sentences.zh: 我在华尔街因参加“艾滋病联合抵制力量”（ACT UP）成立一周年纪念活动而被捕。

sentences.en: What was the next big public action that you took with ACT UP?
sentences.zh: 你和ACT UP一起采取的下一个重大公开行动是什么？

sentences.en: The FDA, the Food and Drug Administration.
sentences.zh: 是FDA，即美国食品药品监督管理局。

sentences.en: October 11, 1988.
It lasted all day.
sentences.zh: 活动持续了一整天。

sentences.en: There were over 1,000 demonstrators from ACT UP chapters in Rockville, Maryland, surrounding the Food and Drug Administration.
sentences.zh: 来自马里兰州罗克维尔市ACT UP分会的1000多名示威者包围了食品药品监督管理局。

sentences.en: We're here today, we're straight.
sentences.zh: 我们今天来到这里，我们是直率的。

sentences.en: We're here today because we want to make a difference.
sentences.zh: 我们今天来到这里是因为我们想有所作为。

sentences.en: We're here today because we care.
sentences.zh: 我们今天来到这里是因为我们在乎。

sentences.en: And it was surrounded by hundreds of police officers.
sentences.zh: 那里被数百名警察包围了。

sentences.en: I see some of your men are wearing plastic gloves.
sentences.zh: 我看到你们有些人戴着塑料手套。

sentences.en: Did the department provide them?
sentences.zh: 是部门提供的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: That's up to the individual officers to whether he wants to wear them or does not want to wear them.
sentences.zh: 这取决于警员个人是否想戴，或者不想戴。

sentences.en: Whatever made him feel comfortable.
sentences.zh: 怎么让他觉得舒服就怎么来。

sentences.en: And, you know, I wanted to do something that would get my fellow activists riled up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想做点能让我的同伴们激动起来的事情。

sentences.en: I had noticed this overhang over the front door and I was trying to figure out how I could get past 30 cops to get up onto that.
sentences.zh: 我注意到前门上方有个悬挑结构，我一直在想怎么绕过那30个警察爬上去。

sentences.en: And so me and two friends just walked towards them like we wanted to negotiate or talk with them.
sentences.zh: 于是我和两个朋友径直朝他们走去，装作要和他们谈判或交谈的样子。

sentences.en: And we came within about six feet of the front line, which was just below the outer edge of the overhang.
sentences.zh: 我们走到离前线大约六英尺的地方，那里就在悬挑结构外缘的下方。

sentences.en: And just when we got there, my friends clasped their hands together and I put my right foot in and I was launched.
sentences.zh: 就在我们到达那里时，我的朋友们双手紧扣，我把右脚踩上去，然后被弹射了出去。

sentences.en: Just as the cops sprang forward trying to catch me.
sentences.zh: 就在警察冲过来试图抓住我的时候。

sentences.en: And I started hanging this huge banner that said silence equals death over the front entrance of the FDA.
sentences.zh: 我开始在FDA正门上方悬挂那条巨大的横幅，上面写着“沉默等于死亡”。

sentences.en: And all the activists converged at the front door and started cheering and hooting and hollering.
sentences.zh: 所有的活动人士都汇聚到前门，开始欢呼、起哄和呐喊。

sentences.en: It was very symbolic of how we were seizing the building that day.
sentences.zh: 这非常有象征意义，代表了我们那天是如何占领这座大楼的。

sentences.en: For many Americans, it was the first time they had seen large numbers of gay men and lesbians taking to the streets and determined and angry and unified.
sentences.zh: 对许多美国人来说，这是他们第一次看到如此多同性恋男性和女性走上街头，表现得坚定、愤怒且团结一致。

sentences.en: I think we destroyed the American myth that the homosexual is weak and timid and when threatened will cower in a corner.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们打破了美国人的迷思，即同性恋者是软弱胆小的，受到威胁时只会缩在角落里。

sentences.en: And what was your message to the FDA in that moment when you are scaling the building and unfurling this sign that says silence equals death?
sentences.zh: 当你爬上大楼并展开那条写着“沉默等于死亡”的标语时，你那一刻想传达给FDA的信息是什么？

sentences.en: We wanted them to create an entirely different regulatory scheme for how they analyzed drugs for life-threatening illnesses like AIDS versus other drugs.
sentences.zh: 我们希望他们为分析艾滋病等危及生命的疾病药物制定一套完全不同的监管方案，而不是沿用其他药物的方案。

sentences.en: We wanted them to work proactively with pharmaceutical companies to speed the development of drugs, to make sure that their clinical trials
sentences.zh: 我们希望他们能与制药公司积极合作，加快药物研发，确保临床试验

sentences.en: would enroll quickly and get data quickly.
sentences.zh: 能快速招募受试者并快速获取数据。

sentences.en: We wanted them to approve drugs as soon as possible and we wanted them to open up a mechanism whereby people who weren't in the clinical trials
sentences.zh: 我们希望他们尽快批准药物，并希望他们建立一种机制，让那些没有参加临床试验的人

sentences.en: could still access some experimental therapies before they were approved.
sentences.zh: 也能在药物获批前获得一些实验性疗法。

sentences.en: And to our amazement, within about a year of that action, we got almost all of that out of the FDA.
sentences.zh: 令我们惊讶的是，在那次行动后大约一年内，我们从FDA那里得到了几乎所有这些要求。

sentences.en: We may not have convinced Americans to love us
sentences.zh: 我们可能没能说服美国人爱我们，

sentences.en: or to tolerate us, but Americans do not like to hear that their own government is letting thousands of their own citizens die.
sentences.zh: 或者容忍我们，但美国人不喜欢听到自己的政府正任由成千上万的公民死去。

sentences.en: When the living can no longer speak,
sentences.zh: 当生者无法再发声时，

sentences.en: the dead may speak for them.
sentences.zh: 死者或许能为他们代言。

sentences.en: So by 91 or 92, we're an incredibly busy movement with almost weekly demonstrations, but every week we start our Monday night meetings
sentences.zh: 到了91或92年，我们已经是一个极其忙碌的运动，几乎每周都有示威活动，但每周我们开始周一晚上的会议时，

sentences.en: with an announcement of who had died that week.
sentences.zh: 都会宣布那一周有谁去世了。

sentences.en: I'd like to read something that Mark wrote and wants us to do today very mysteriously.
sentences.zh: 我想读一些马克写的东西，他希望我们今天以非常神秘的方式去做。

sentences.en: And all of us are going to memorials every month.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人每个月都要参加追悼会。

sentences.en: Several months before his death,
sentences.zh: 在他去世前几个月，

sentences.en: Mark said, I want my funeral to be fierce and defiant.
sentences.zh: 马克说，我希望我的葬礼是激烈而反抗的。

sentences.en: So we were winning all these battles, but we were losing the war.
sentences.zh: 所以我们赢得了所有这些战斗，但我们却输掉了整场战争。

sentences.en: The death count just kept rising and rising.
sentences.zh: 死亡人数一直在不断攀升。

sentences.en: Let the whole earth hear us now.
sentences.zh: 让全世界现在就听到我们的声音。

sentences.en: Now, we beg, we pray, we demand that this epidemic end.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们恳求、祈祷、要求这场流行病结束。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: We just gave up on the idea that we were going to find a cure.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚放弃了寻找治愈方法的想法。

sentences.en: The virus was just too complex.
sentences.zh: 病毒实在太复杂了。

sentences.en: But we were hoping to shake out enough drugs that we could find a magic combination that would add up to real time, added to people's lives.
sentences.zh: 但我们希望能筛选出足够的药物，找到一种神奇的组合，能为人们的生命增加真正的时间。

sentences.en: That was our new hope in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 那是我们在90年代初的新希望。

sentences.en: And we kept fighting for that and fighting for that.
sentences.zh: 我们为此不断抗争，不断抗争。

sentences.en: And finally, finally, we got lucky.
sentences.zh: 最后，终于，我们幸运了。

sentences.en: We came to the conclusion that it's inevitable for HIV to develop drug resistance if you give it one drug at a time.
sentences.zh: 我们得出的结论是，如果你一次只给一种药，HIV产生耐药性是不可避免的。

sentences.en: However, if you start to combine the drugs and try to force the virus into a corner using multiple drugs, it is exceedingly difficult for HIV to become...
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你开始联合用药，试图用多种药物将病毒逼入绝境，HIV就极难……

sentences.en: In 1996, scientists announced that if you use three drugs at the same time, that was the magic number, you could stop the replication of HIV in a patient.
sentences.zh: 1996年，科学家宣布，如果你同时使用三种药物，这就是那个神奇的数字，你就能阻止HIV在患者体内复制。

sentences.en: By spring of 1996, we had three different trials using a protease inhibitor plus two other drugs.
sentences.zh: 到1996年春天，我们有三个不同的试验，使用了蛋白酶抑制剂加上其他两种药物。

sentences.en: And Dr. David Ho, who was very involved with this discovery and presented the data...
sentences.zh: 戴维·何医生（Dr. David Ho）非常深入地参与了这一发现并展示了数据……

sentences.en: We knew that unlike previous experience, the virus was coming under good control and staying there.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，与以往的经验不同，病毒得到了很好的控制，并且保持住了。

sentences.en: He started speculating that if patients stayed on these regimens, that maybe the immune system would knock out the rest of the virus on its own over time.
sentences.zh: 他开始推测，如果患者坚持这些方案，也许免疫系统随着时间的推移能自行清除剩余的病毒。

sentences.en: And so we were pretty excited.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时非常兴奋。

sentences.en: These current regimens might lead to what they called eradication, i.e. cure.
sentences.zh: 这些当前的方案可能会导致他们所说的根除，即治愈。

sentences.en: And we're talking to ourselves and we're saying, what if this is real?
sentences.zh: 我们当时在自言自语，说，如果这是真的呢？

sentences.en: And we just couldn't believe it after all this time.
sentences.zh: 经历了这么久，我们简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: We all started on these triple drug regimens and within three months, we were all undetectable.
sentences.zh: 我们都开始使用这些三联药物方案，三个月内，我们体内的病毒都检测不到了。

sentences.en: Then it was like, wow, this is it.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，哇，就是这个了。

sentences.en: This is huge.
sentences.zh: 这太重大了。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The death rate in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国的死亡率

sentences.en: over the next two years dropped by 75%.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的两年里下降了75%。

sentences.en: Just a huge shift in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这在疫情中是一个巨大的转变。

sentences.en: But did it mean that HIV was really being eradicated from your system?
sentences.zh: 但这是否意味着HIV真的从你的系统中被根除了？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: But it took us a couple years to figure that out.
sentences.zh: 但我们花了几年时间才弄明白这一点。

sentences.en: And they started learning more and more about how even wilier this virus is and how it is able to protect itself and hide in your body in all sorts of cellular compartments.
sentences.zh: 他们开始越来越多地了解到这种病毒是多么狡猾，它是如何保护自己并隐藏在人体内各种细胞隔室中的。

sentences.en: It hides in cells that line your GI tract.
sentences.zh: 它隐藏在消化道内壁的细胞里。

sentences.en: It hides in your brain.
sentences.zh: 它隐藏在你的大脑里。

sentences.en: It hides in macrophage cells.
sentences.zh: 它隐藏在巨噬细胞里。

sentences.en: The basic science that started following from this was endlessly depressing.
sentences.zh: 随后展开的基础科学研究让人感到无尽的沮丧。

sentences.en: And within, I would say, five years, the talk of cure had just vanished.
sentences.zh: 我想在五年内，关于治愈的讨论就彻底消失了。

sentences.en: So, by the time we get to 2007, there is no cure research going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，到了2007年，已经没有任何关于治愈的研究在进行了。

sentences.en: Everybody's kind of resigned to the fact that the virus is too wily and has too many hiding places in the body to get it out.
sentences.zh: 每个人都默认了一个事实，即这种病毒太狡猾了，在体内有太多的藏身之处，无法将其彻底清除。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, this news breaks.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，这个新闻爆出来了。

sentences.en: He is the only person ever to be cured of HIV and AIDS.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一一个被治愈HIV和艾滋病的人。

sentences.en: But his cure was somewhat of an accident.
sentences.zh: 但他的治愈在某种程度上是一次意外。

sentences.en: That somebody has been cured of AIDS.
sentences.zh: 有人被治愈了艾滋病。

sentences.en: And it's like, what?
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉是，什么？

sentences.en: The only man believed ever to have been cured of HIV spoke today at the International AIDS Conference in Washington.
sentences.zh: 唯一被认为治愈了HIV的男子今天在华盛顿举行的国际艾滋病大会上发言。

sentences.en: His name is Timothy Brown.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫蒂莫西·布朗（Timothy Brown）。

sentences.en: He's also known as the Berlin Patient.
sentences.zh: 他也被称为“柏林病人”。

sentences.en: They had this fellow called the Berlin Patient.
sentences.zh: 他们有这个叫“柏林病人”的家伙。

sentences.en: Doctors in Germany used an experimental radiation treatment to wipe out Brown's immune system.
sentences.zh: 德国的医生使用了一种实验性放射疗法来摧毁布朗的免疫系统。

sentences.en: They gave him two bone marrow transplants, and the results were remarkable.
sentences.zh: 他们给他做了两次骨髓移植，结果非常显著。

sentences.en: Who also was suffering from very advanced cancer.
sentences.zh: 他当时也患有非常晚期的癌症。

sentences.en: Doctors in Germany wiped out his immune system with chemotherapy and radiation, and then gave him two rounds of stem cell transplants.
sentences.zh: 德国的医生用化疗和放疗摧毁了他的免疫系统，然后给他进行了两轮干细胞移植。

sentences.en: His bone marrow donor had a rare gene mutation that made the donor, and now Brown's, stem cells resistant to HIV.
sentences.zh: 他的骨髓捐赠者有一种罕见的基因突变，使捐赠者，也就是现在的布朗，其干细胞对HIV具有抵抗力。

sentences.en: This new immune system grew out of this bone marrow, and it worked.
sentences.zh: 这个新的免疫系统从骨髓中生长出来，而且起作用了。

sentences.en: If there was any HIV hiding anywhere in his body, it had nothing to latch onto in order to replicate.
sentences.zh: 如果他体内有任何隐藏的HIV，它在体内找不到任何可以附着并进行复制的地方。

sentences.en: And so it died.
sentences.zh: 所以它死了。

sentences.en: And so it died.
sentences.zh: 所以它死了。

sentences.en: So the idea is that this person who was immune to HIV, that if you take their bone marrow and introduce it into the system of an HIV-positive person, the Berlin Patient.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法是，这个对HIV免疫的人，如果你提取他们的骨髓并引入到HIV阳性者的系统中，就像“柏林病人”那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the Berlin Patient's immune system starts to develop around that bone marrow that's immune to HIV, that the entire patient becomes immune to HIV.
sentences.zh: 而“柏林病人”的免疫系统开始围绕那个对HIV免疫的骨髓发育，整个患者就变得对HIV免疫了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so that just cracked open everybody's imaginations.
sentences.zh: 这一下子打开了所有人的想象力。

sentences.en: And Cure Research was back on the agenda.
sentences.zh: 治愈研究又回到了议程上。

sentences.en: A whole field of research was born trying to figure out how we could do this without wiping out a person's immune system first, without a bone marrow transplant.
sentences.zh: 一个全新的研究领域诞生了，试图找出如何在不先摧毁一个人免疫系统的情况下，在没有骨髓移植的情况下做到这一点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because it would be almost impossible to replicate this on a big scale.
sentences.zh: 因为在大规模范围内复制这一点几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And there were other attempts to replicate what happened with Timothy Brown and the Berlin Patient.
sentences.zh: 还有其他尝试来复制蒂莫西·布朗和“柏林病人”身上发生的事情。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, they failed.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，它们失败了。

sentences.en: They tried this in other people with HIV that had cancer that needed bone marrow transplants.
sentences.zh: 他们在其他需要骨髓移植的HIV癌症患者身上尝试过。

sentences.en: There was a period of time where it looked like they had undetectable HIV after the transplant, but then it bounced back.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间看起来他们在移植后HIV检测不到了，但后来又反弹了。

sentences.en: And so there were some disappointments.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有一些失望。

sentences.en: And so what happened two weeks ago...
sentences.zh: 那么两周前发生了什么……

sentences.en: Researchers say the latest success confirms that a cure for HIV infection is possible.
sentences.zh: 研究人员表示，最新的成功证实了治愈HIV感染是可能的。

sentences.en: ...was proof that what happened in the Berlin Patient was not a fluke.
sentences.zh: ……证明了“柏林病人”身上发生的事情并非偶然。

sentences.en: It comes 12 years after American Timothy Brown, known as the Berlin Patient, became the first known adult to be cured.
sentences.zh: 这距离美国人蒂莫西·布朗（即“柏林病人”）成为首位已知的被治愈成年人已经过去了12年。

sentences.en: Both patients underwent stem cell transplants from donors who carried a rare genetic mutation that made them resistant to HIV.
sentences.zh: 两名患者都接受了来自携带罕见基因突变捐赠者的干细胞移植，这种突变使他们对HIV具有抵抗力。

sentences.en: Doctors say the second successful...
sentences.zh: 医生说，第二次成功的……

sentences.en: You know, we're not rushing to the hospital to get bone marrow transplants.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们并没有冲向医院去接受骨髓移植。

sentences.en: But I was thrilled to hear this news, mostly because I think it's going to probably get us quicker to that day when we ultimately find a gene therapy that does the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但我很高兴听到这个消息，主要是因为我认为这可能会让我们更快地迎来最终找到能实现同样效果的基因疗法的那一天。

sentences.en: Peter, your entire adult life has been focused on advancing treatment for HIV and AIDS.
sentences.zh: 彼得，你整个成年生活都专注于推进HIV和艾滋病的治疗。

sentences.en: And it's remarkable how much advancement has occurred and that you've witnessed.
sentences.zh: 你所见证的进步之大令人瞩目。

sentences.en: If you live long enough to experience a cure, and of course, we all hope you do, what will you do then?
sentences.zh: 如果你活得足够长，能亲眼见证治愈的那一天，当然我们都希望你能，到那时你会做什么？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, since 2008, I really do love the idea that I'm probably going to be there when it happens, that I'm going to witness that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，自2008年以来，我真的很喜欢这个想法，即我可能真的会在现场见证那一刻。

sentences.en: I just want to be there, if they ever do find a cure.
sentences.zh: 如果他们真的找到了治愈方法，我只想在现场。

sentences.en: Imagine what it would be like.
sentences.zh: 想象一下那会是什么样子。

sentences.en: It's going to be like that last scene in Long Time Companion, that great AIDS film, where the dream sequence at the end of the movie,
sentences.zh: 那会像那部伟大的艾滋病电影《长相伴》（Long Time Companion）的最后一个场景，电影结尾的梦境片段，

sentences.en: where all the people who have died of AIDS come back and celebrate on a sunny day on the beach on Fire Island.
sentences.zh: 所有死于艾滋病的人都回来，在火岛（Fire Island）阳光明媚的海滩上庆祝。

sentences.en: And everybody's partying.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在狂欢。

sentences.en: It's like a big gay disco.
sentences.zh: 就像一场盛大的同性恋迪斯科。

sentences.en: It's everybody we've lost, but it's everybody we've lost, and they're just celebrating.
sentences.zh: 那是我们失去的所有人，但那是我们失去的所有人，他们只是在庆祝。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: It will.
sentences.zh: 会的。

sentences.en: It's me.
sentences.zh: 是我。

sentences.en: It might be like that, you know.
sentences.zh: 也许情况就是那样，你知道的。

sentences.en: You know, I'm going to be an ex-AIDS activiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我打算不再做艾滋病活动家了。

sentences.en: And I'm going to do something else and be glad for it and be proud.
sentences.zh: 我要去做点别的事，并为此感到高兴和自豪。

sentences.en: I hope that you will be an ex-AIDS activist, Peter, and I look forward to chatting with you when that day comes.
sentences.zh: 彼得，我希望你也能不再做艾滋病活动家，我期待着那一天到来时能和你聊天。

sentences.en: Yeah, me too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也是。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Peter Staley is now directing his activism toward greater awareness and access to a drug, Truvada,
sentences.zh: 彼得·斯塔利现在正将他的行动重点转向提高人们对一种名为“舒发泰”药物的认识和获取途径，

sentences.en: that is 99% effective in preventing HIV infections, but remains unaffordable to large numbers of people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这种药在预防艾滋病毒感染方面有99%的有效性，但在美国仍有大量民众负担不起，

sentences.en: and the world, where HIV infections are on the rise.
sentences.zh: 在世界范围内也是如此，而艾滋病毒感染率正在上升。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: In New Zealand on Wednesday, the first funerals began for victims of last week's attack on two mosques.
sentences.zh: 周三，新西兰开始为上周两座清真寺袭击事件的遇难者举行首批葬礼。

sentences.en: In Christchurch, the bodies of a father and son killed in the attacks,
sentences.zh: 在基督城，在袭击中丧生的一对父子，

sentences.en: 16-year-old Hamza Mustafa and 44-year-old Khaled Mustafa, were wrapped in white cloths and carried to their graves in open caskets on the shoulders of mourners.
sentences.zh: 16岁的哈姆扎·穆斯塔法和44岁的哈立德·穆斯塔法，他们的遗体被白布包裹，在哀悼者的肩上被抬入敞开的棺材，送往墓地。

sentences.en: Inshallah, brothers, everybody will get a chance to get the families in firSt.
sentences.zh: 因沙安拉（真主保佑），兄弟们，每个人都会有机会让家属先来。

sentences.en: Let the brothers carry in their bodies firSt.
sentences.zh: 让兄弟们先抬着遗体进去。

sentences.en: Let them lower the person inside the grave, inshallah, and we will all participate.
sentences.zh: 让他们把人放进墓穴里，因沙安拉，我们大家都会参与。

sentences.en: Among those mourners was 13-year-old Zaid Mustafa, who came to bury his brother and father, and who was himself shot in the leg during the attack.
sentences.zh: 在哀悼者中，13岁的扎伊德·穆斯塔法也在场，他来安葬他的哥哥和父亲，而他自己在袭击中腿部也受了伤。

sentences.en: And then having the son stand over his father and brother, he himself wounded, and to farewell and say to his father,
sentences.zh: 看着那个儿子站在他父亲和哥哥的遗体旁，他自己还带着伤，向他的父亲告别并说，

sentences.en: I don't want to be here alone.
sentences.zh: 我不想一个人留在这里。

sentences.en: That was devastating.
sentences.zh: 那真是令人心碎。

sentences.en: And a federal judge has ruled that the Trump administration violated federal law by failing to account for climate change
sentences.zh: 一位联邦法官裁定，特朗普政府在开放数十万英亩联邦土地用于石油和天然气钻探时，

sentences.en: when it opened hundreds of thousands of acres of federal lands to oil and gas drilling.
sentences.zh: 未能考虑气候变化的影响，违反了联邦法律。

sentences.en: The judge faulted the Department of the Interior for not assessing how the drilling projects, which are in Wyoming, contribute to the country's overall carbon output,
sentences.zh: 法官指责内政部没有评估这些位于怀俄明州的钻探项目如何影响该国的总体碳排放量，

sentences.en: which he said was required by law.
sentences.zh: 他表示这是法律所要求的。

sentences.en: The ruling, which temporarily blocks the drilling in Wyoming, could offer environmentalists a legal playbook for challenging Trump's entire oil and gas agenda.
sentences.zh: 这项裁决暂时阻止了怀俄明州的钻探活动，可能为环保人士挑战特朗普整个石油和天然气议程提供了一套法律策略。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Special thanks to David France, the director of How to Survive a Plague.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢《瘟疫求生指南》的导演大卫·弗朗斯。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在任何你收听播客的地方订阅收听。
